critical_code_review_comments: test_security_invariants.py is a clean, well-scoped guard module. Parametrisation is explicit, fixtures are module-scoped (fast), and the two-fold defence (JSON-quoted-key substring + bcrypt regex) is a solid mix of structural + value-level checks.

TestSensitivityRegistry.test_admin_service_lists_all_known_credential_fields greps the file source rather than importing the constant. That is fragile to refactors (e.g., moving SENSITIVE_USER_FIELDS into a shared module). Consider `from domains.admin.service import SENSITIVE_USER_FIELDS` and asserting set membership — same guarantee, refactor-safe.

USER_SELF_ENDPOINTS test currently accepts any status code (200 or 4xx) and only scans the body — that is intentional per the docstring (consent_required 403 is legitimate). Good documented decision, no change needed.
The admin-read scan asserts 200 for BOTH admin AND support on every listed endpoint. This double-confirms Phase-6's 'support = read-only' contract as a side effect. Nice.

Consider adding /api/v1/admin/users/{id} explicitly to ADMIN_READ_ENDPOINTS (currently covered by TestAdminUserDetailDeepScan but not in the flat list) so the invariants matrix is a single source of truth. Low priority.
